llm.summary: This speech-service skill is transparent about its behavior, but its shared server file store and admin endpoints can expose or delete data if deployed without strong access controls.

dimensions.detail: The default examples can bind the service broadly, authentication is opt-in, URL downloads are server-side with private-network blocking disabled by default, and staged files persist indefinitely unless cleaned up.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Setup uses ordinary Docker run commands, curl examples, and an optional helper script; no hidden installer, persistence hook, or obfuscated install behavior was found in the inspected artifacts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill gives guardrails, but the documented /v1/files namespace is globally listable/readable/deletable by any API caller and the model unload endpoints affect shared service state; this is broad authority for agent-accessible workflows.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Server-side staged uploads and URL-download cache entries persist under the talkies data directory until explicit deletion, and deletion is irreversible in a shared unisolated namespace.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The ASR/TTS purpose matches the documented capabilities: outbound requests to a configured talkies server, transcription, speech generation, URL fetching, server-side staging, MCP ASR tools, and optional model management.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you will point the skill at a talkies instance you run or explicitly trust. Enable TALKIES_AUTH_TOKEN, prefer loopback or protected network exposure, avoid staging sensitive media on shared deployments, do not let agents browse or bulk-delete /v1/files, and reserve unload/model-eviction calls for explicit maintenance tasks.
llm.findings:
[TM1] expected: The /v1/files delete capability is documented and supports staging cleanup, but the artifact confirms it is shared, unisolated, irreversible, and not protected by per-caller ownership.
[TM1] expected: The /api/ps and /unload endpoints are documented as resource-management operations, but they can disrupt other users on a shared instance and the skill says not to invoke them without explicit administrative intent.
[TM1] expected: The server-side staging concerns are not hidden; the skill repeatedly warns that files are enumerable/readable/deletable by anyone with API access and recommends auth, cleanup, and deployment-level isolation.
